title: Adaptive Preflight Proxy Adapter and Staged Upgrade Windowing for Isolated Deploys
creator: Maya Chen
description: Customers with strict network isolation or legacy perimeter proxies request non-invasive preflight adapters and precise upgrade windows. This ticket defines a triage flow and productized adapter pattern that lets on-prem/VPC customers install a lightweight proxy adapter (customer-controlled) for bootstrap connectivity checks, then schedule staged kernel/agent upgrades in narrow maintenance windows. Goals: reduce manual engineering time during intake, lower rollback risk for air-gapped installs, and create deterministic comms/SLAs for upgrade gates.
acceptance_criteria: A documented preflight adapter spec with supported proxy types (HTTP CONNECT, TLS passthrough, SOCKS, corporate forward proxy) and config templates
An intake scoring rubric that classifies network risk and maps customers to one of three upgrade lanes (self-service, assisted, concierge)
A small reference adapter binary/container and Helm manifest that customers can deploy to run automated probes and collect anonymized connectivity diagnostics
Console UI: a per-customer upgrade runway page showing allowed maintenance windows, last successful preflight, and rollback plan
Runbook and escalation paths documented in Confluence and linked to support playbooks

decision_log: 2025-12-12: Decided to ship a read-only adapter that performs probes and uploads signed telemetry only; no remote exec or auto-upgrade capability.
2026-01-15: Chose three upgrade lanes to balance customer autonomy vs. support cost; concierge lane reserved for high-risk customers and enterprise SLA customers.
2026-02-02: Agreed on default 4-hour maintenance windows for assisted lane; self-service customers can request narrower windows via intake form.
risks: Customers may refuse to run any container due to air-gap policies — mitigation: offer offline probe bundle and manual log ingestion flow
Proxy diversity (legacy appliances) may produce false negatives in probes — mitigation: extend probe set and capture verbose packet-level traces when permitted
Telemetry and PII exposure risk — mitigation: telemetry contract with strict allowlist and signing; legal sign-off required
